title: Review: Diffraction grating; Wave–particle duality; Boundary behaviour of waves
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W09-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; W09-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: Q03-1#N.4a, Q03-uk1#N.7, W09-1#N.4a, W19-1#N.11, Q03-1#N.17b, Q03-uk1#N.8, W09-1#N.10, W19-1#N.3, Q03-uk1#N.3, W09-1#N.8a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electron diffraction
items.clue: Bright concentric rings on a fluorescent screen after a beam passes through thin graphite.

items.label: Wave–particle duality
items.clue: Idea that light and matter each need two models, and the experiment decides which one shows.

items.label: Path difference
items.clue: Extra distance d sin θ for light from the next opening; a whole number of λ gives a bright beam.

items.label: Diffraction grating
items.clue: Plate with many equally spaced, parallel openings that sends bright beams at certain angles only.

questions.stem: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 2.0 kV. Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, m_e = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the electron as non-relativistic. What is the de Broglie wavelength of the electron?
A team wants to resolve detail of about 10⁻¹⁶ m, a tenth of the size of a nucleon. At these energies, an electron's energy ≈ momentum × c. Roughly what electron energy do they need?

options.text: About 1 GeV
About 100 GeV
About 10 GeV
About 0.1 GeV

questions.explanation: p = h/λ = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ ÷ 10⁻¹⁶ = 6.6 × 10⁻¹⁸ kg m s⁻¹. Energy ≈ pc = 2.0 × 10⁻⁹ J ≈ 12 GeV: about 10 GeV.

questions.stem: Light of wavelength 650 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating that has 600 lines per millimetre. At what angle to the straight-through direction is the second-order maximum observed?
At night, a person in a brightly lit room sees a faint reflection of the room in the window, while people outside can see into the room through the same window. What does this show?

options.text: Glass reflects light only at night; by day it transmits all the light.
Glass transmits all the light; the faint image is light scattered by dust.
Light going from air into glass is reflected; light going from glass into air is transmitted.
At each glass surface, part of the light is reflected, part transmitted.

questions.explanation: The speed of light changes at the boundary, so the wave splits: a small part is reflected (the faint image) and most is transmitted (seen from outside).

questions.stem: A beam of electrons and a beam of protons are each accelerated from rest through 100 V and aimed at the same crystal, whose rows of atoms are 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m apart. Which beam shows clear diffraction?

options.text: Only the protons: they are heavier, so they hit the atoms harder and are scattered more.
Both equally: they have the same charge and the same p.d., so they gain the same energy.
Only the electrons: their wavelength is comparable with the spacing of the atoms.
Neither: diffraction is a property of waves, and both beams are made of particles.

questions.stem: An electron microscope needs electrons with a de Broglie wavelength of 2.5 × 10⁻¹¹ m. Through what potential difference must the electrons be accelerated from rest? Take h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, m = 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and e = 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

options.text: 4.8 kV
50 kV
2.4 kV

questions.stem: A laser beam is directed normally at a grating with 500 lines per mm. On a screen 1.00 m from the grating, the two second-order spots are 1.50 m apart. What is the wavelength of the laser light?

options.text: 750 nm
600 nm
832 nm

questions.stem: Predict first. Sound from a loudspeaker in air reaches the surface of a swimming pool, and sound travels on into the water. Which property of the sound is the same in the water as in the air?

options.text: The distance between its adjacent compressions
The distance it travels in each second
The amount of energy it carries each second
The number of oscillations it makes each second

questions.stem: An electron and a proton have the same kinetic energy, and both move at speeds much less than c. The mass of the proton is about 1840 times the mass of the electron. How do their de Broglie wavelengths compare?

options.text: The proton's wavelength is about 43 times as long as the electron's.
The electron's wavelength is about 1840 times the proton's.
The electron's wavelength is about 43 times the proton's.
They have equal wavelengths, as the particles have equal energies.

questions.stem: Predict first. White light is incident normally on a diffraction grating. Which describes the pattern seen on a screen?

options.text: A white central maximum, with a spectrum in each order on either side and violet nearest the centre
A white central maximum, with a spectrum in each order on either side and red nearest the centre
A spectrum at the centre, as well as in each order on either side, with violet nearest to the centre
A white central maximum and a white maximum in each order, as all colours share the same angles
